key_insight: Reference Forcing targets identity and background drift in long video generation through region-guided drift correction. The provided abstract is incomplete, so the precise correction mechanism and results are not available.
problem_solved: Autoregressive video models trained with distribution matching distillation over short windows may lose subject and background consistency over longer sequences. Retaining or retrieving KV-cache history cannot fully address this when that history has already drifted.
method: Proposes Reference Forcing, described in the title as region-guided drift correction for long video generation.
Targets accumulated subject and background inconsistencies rather than relying solely on potentially drifted cached history.
Implementation details, training objectives, and evaluation results are not included in the supplied excerpt.
impact: The approach aims to make long generated videos more visually consistent without sacrificing natural motion. Its practical effectiveness and computational costs cannot be assessed from the incomplete abstract.

Conceptual frame with separate subject and background regions highlighted.

paper_title: Reference Forcing: Long Video Generation with Region-Guided Drift Correction
paper_authors: Sheng Zhao, Haitian Zheng, Weikai Lin, Junjie Zhao, Yuhao Zhu
